Current workforce dynamics are characterized by a flow of constant changes where factors such as globalization and rapid advances in technology are provoking disruptive changes in most companies. While adapting to change can become quite challenging for some of your employees, your goal is to effectively support your employees when navigating through changes and provide them with the information and resources necessary to experience a positive transition.   

### Explain the why 
Lack of information is definitely damaging for the health of your team and your organization. Employees who understand the context and reasoning behind changes are less resistant to change. Make sure to dedicate time to discuss why a given change is important and the kind of transformation that is expected to occur. Keeping your team informed is a critical task to clarify their doubts and learn how they are doing in their adaptation process. Read this [article](https://hbr.org/2018/10/dont-just-tell-employees-organizational-changes-are-coming-explain-why) to learn additional information on how to explain the why to your team. 

### Maintain engagement in the process
Once employees are aware a change is coming, you can assist them to stay engaged and committed to the process. To do this, you can provide them with resources such as instruction guides and training sessions. Also, be sure to ask for their feedback on the process (especially if the change has a direct effect on their everyday processes) and communicate updates on a timely manner. 

### Remember everyone is different 
Change can affect each team member in a different way. Offering ongoing support and starting conversations on how they are processing the change can help your employees feel more empowered through the process. 

Read this [article](https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbescoachescouncil/2016/12/21/10-ways-managers-can-help-employees-adjust-to-change/#78dcbb024161) for additional recommendations on how to help employees adjust to change.
